Commentary.Commentary: A leather-hunting it has been for the Kiwis, toiling hard for 162.5 overs. England bowlers will be fresh and aiming to come out hard - but on a hot and humid day, on a pitch which has nothing to offer, they will have to toil hard to take 10 wickets. But if they get the Kiwis 5 down tonight, we could have a game on our hands. Stay tuned for the final session of the day.

The last 35 balls make the reading good for New Zealand, as they tell about a collapse. But in reality, England just threw it away. They went for quick runs and perished. The session has belonged to the duo of Root and Pope, whose 193-run stand has taken the team to safety. Question is, is it good enough to enforce a result? Mind you, the forecast is very poor for Tuesday.

Fruitful session for both teams in terms of the runs and the wickets but England would be very, very happy. A lead of 101 and even though one would say momentum is with New Zealand, that lead is very, very significant. Around 35 overs left in the day and the visitors will aim for at least 4 wickets and in that, Kane Williamson for sure.

OUT! TIMBER! England have been bowled out! From 455/5 to 476 all out, this has been a big collapse but England will not mind it that much. Wagner bowls a slower full toss on off, it is swerving in. Broad goes onto the back foot looking to defend but is beaten as he might be waiting for the short ball. He brings his bat down late and misses the ball. Wagner hits and Broad has to walk back. This is Neil's 9th 5-wicket haul in Tests and he is pumped after getting toiled for huge parts of the day. England end their innings with a lead of 101 runs and TEA HAS BEEN TAKEN!
Fullish ball on off, Broad blocks it out.
A full toss to welcome Broad! He is surprised and just about manages to fend it back to the bowler.
Stuart Broad walks in at number 11.

OUT! CHOPPED ON! Archer is on his way right after hitting a biggie. Wagner bowls a full length ball just outside off, Archer looks to heave this one over the long on region but gets an inside edge on it. The ball rolls over onto the stumps and Archer has to take the long walk back. England lead by 101 runs.
SIX! Slammed! Good length ball just outside off, Archer makes room and slams this one down the ground over the long on fence for a biggie.
Back of a length ball, Archer looks to pull but the ball goes off the inside half towards mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, Curran cuts this one towards deep point for one.
Curran comes down the track to this length ball, looks to heave but gets an inside edge onto the thigh pads.

Just short! Full ball wide outside off, Curran looks to have a slash at it but the ball goes off the bottom edge on the bounce to Watling.
Tim Southee back into the attack. 36-4-84-2, his figures so far.
Length ball on middle and off, defended out.
Bouncer on middle and leg, Archer gets down in time and lets the ball pass.

Length ball outside off, Jofra leaves it alone.
Yorker just outside off, Curran jams it out towards point and takes a single.
Full ball on middle and off, flicked towards mid-wicket.
A conference going on. Taylor, Williamson, Southee and Watling are involved. Is it about the third new ball? It is due but not taken yet.
Full and around middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Short and outside off, Curran looks to cut but gets a bottom edge which goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Full and outside off, Archer leans and pushes it through the covers for a single to get off the mark.
Tossed up, around leg, pushed back with an open face. Almost carries back to the bowler.
Around off, punched back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
A bouncer around middle, ducked under.
Landed outside off, angling away, left alone.

OUT! Edged and taken! Wickets, all of a sudden! And just when the third new ball is around the corner. Woakes departs as a sacrificial lamb to up the ante. Full and wide outside off, Woakes slashes hard, aiming to go through the covers but can only get a thick outside edge. Simple catch for BJ Watling. England lead by 85.
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Landed outside off, Curran looks to punch but gets a bottom edge towards cover.

Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Outside off, punched off the back foot for a single.
Chris Woakes walks in at number 9, replacing his skipper.

OUT! Caught! The marathon innings ends at last. 226 in 441 balls. 636 minutes at the crease. Boy, have England missed you, Root. They as a team have rarely spent more than 600 minutes at the crease with the bat. New Zealand get 2 wickets in the span of 5 minutes after toiling for more than 3 hours without a scalp. Full and outside off, Root comes down the track and looks to go inside out. But he is not to the pitch of the ball and skews this high in the air. Does not have the distance and Henry Nicholls at sweeper cover runs in to take the catch. Wagner runs towards Root and pats him on the back. Nice sportsmanship. Now, the declaration?
Full and outside off, Root looks to play the reverse sweep but gets hit on the glove. The ball bounces and goes to Watling who fumbles.
Landed outside off, dabbed towards short third man for a single.

OUT! CAUGHT! Stop the press. England have lost a wicket. The 193-run stand has been broken and after 374 balls, a batsman has been dismissed. Selfless shot from Pope. He could have played for his century but he chose his team instead. A short ball, outside off, Ollie looks to pull but gets a top edge, due to the extra bounce. The ball goes high in the air and Jeet Raval takes a simple catch at the ropes near mid-wicket. Well played, young lad.
Full and wide outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
WIDE. Full and miles outside off, almost outside the pitch, Root slashes hard but misses.

Short and outside off, Root pulls it through mid-wicket. Mitchell Santner hares to his right from deep mid-wicket, dives and parries the ball to Jeet Raval running across from deep square leg. Two runs taken. Has Santner hurt himself though? Gets up gingerly and just about tests his knee.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
Full and wide outside off, now Pope plays an agricultural shot, a wild slash across the line but misses.
Neil Wagner now changes his shoes. So, a bit of a delay.
Full and around off, pushed towards long on for a run.  450 UP FOR ENGLAND, lead by 75.
Not all that short, but JR goes back and plays it from there, pulling it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Now the skipper jumps down the track and Santner fires it short and into the body. Joe works it through mid-wicket for how many? Another couple. Moves to 220.
Slower, outside off, Root looks to play the reverse sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. He then deflects it away with his bat as the ball threatens to go back onto the stumps.
Slowly tossed up outside off, Pope initially looks to go big but then adjusts, goes back and dabs it towards point for a single.
Full and around leg, driven back to the bowler. Santner dives to his left to stop.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Outside off, played through point for a single.

FOUR! TAKE THAT! A length ball outside off, Pope shuffles across and hammers it straight back. Root at the other end has to get out of the way as the ball comes straight at him. He evades it though and the cherry races to the long off fence.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
Short and wide outside off, Root reaches out and cuts it towards cover.

DROPPED! But a tough chance. Very tough chance. Full and around off, Root hammers this straight back. Poor Wagner barely has any time to react but manages to stick out his left hand. That is good reflex else his left knee would have been a goner. The ball goes to cover while Wagner is on the floor. Brave man. Strong man. Gets up in a trice and smiles. What does he have for supper?
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

DRINKS! Another hour where England have dominated. A double ton for Joe Root, a half ton for Ollie Pope, all these milestones coming in this hour. New Zealand have tried their best but luck has just not favoured them with numerous near misses. The only question that now remains is what total do England have in mind before they declare. Also, some good news regarding the weather as the sun has now come out and we can see the ground bathed in sunshine.

MISSES THE HELMET! Not of Root's, but the one behind the keeper. Nearly 5 penalty runs. Landed outside off, Joe looks to cut but gets a bottom edge. The ball bounces, past the off stump and poor Watling, for the umpteenth time today, has to dive to his left to stop the ball. It was heading straight to the helmet kept behind. Cannot stop it cleanly and parries it behind. Another couple taken.

Full and wide outside off, Pope reaches out to steer it to third man but gets a bottom edge which goes on the bounce to the keeper.

Around off, pushed towards mid on.

Full and around middle, Root tickles it through square leg. Matt Henry gives it a good chase from fine leg, slides to his left and saves the boundary. Another couple taken. THIS IS NOW THE HIGHEST INDIVIDUAL SCORE at this venue. England lead by 41 now.
Length ball just outside off, dabbed towards the off side.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.

200 FOR JOE ROOT! The English skipper has stepped up to the plate and recovered his best form. Good length ball on off, Root defends this one with soft hands towards the off side. The fielder from cover runs in and throws the ball at the keeper's end while diving. Had he hit, Ollie Pope would have been gone for all money despite a dive. That was a risk worth taking though as this has helped the skipper reach his double ton. Joe Root has now become just the 2nd player to score a double ton at this venue, the previous man being his counterpart, Kane Williamson against Bangladesh in February 2019. Records tumbling!

It is now the highest score by a visiting batsman on this ground, going past Rahul Dravid's 190 in 1999.

The physiotherapist comes out now. Has a check on Southee. Is the heat and humidity getting to the bowler? There is a bowling change as well. Not what we anticipated. Daryl Mitchell it will be. 19-5-50-0 so far.

50 up for Ollie Pope! It has been a great innings by him as he has supported his skipper very well. Shortish outside off, Pope goes back and cuts this towards point. Pope pushes this one straight to the man at cover.

Root opens the face of the bat and guides this one straight to short third man.

Drags it back, outside off. Pope cuts it to the man at point.

Mitchell Santner to bowl from the other end. 27-4-64-0 so far.

Good length ball this time, just outside off, pushed towards cover.

Gathering. New Zealand at the boundary line. Rain clouds above. The conditions were overcast in the morning and they seem to have become even more so now. Kane Williamson is giving a pep talk to his team and he is either smiling or his face is just like that. Out come Root and Pope. Tim Southee to begin proceedings post Lunch. 32-4-75-2 so far. Root to face. Here we go...
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

38.2 overs, 110 runs and no wickets lost. What a session this has been for England! They have taken things by the scruff of the neck and eased their way into a lead when everyone was ruling them out early on in their innings. The Kiwi bowlers have bowled with a lot of discipline and induced a lot of edges but the England batters have rode their luck. But just like the saying goes, fortune favours the brave and it has favoured Root and Pope. They are amidst an unbeaten 117-run stand and and will be looking to score runs at a better run rate now with the pressure off their shoulders. With Root looking to go for the double ton and Pope for his ton, runs are surely on offer. Join us after the Lunch break at 1340 Local (0040 GMT) for all the action.

DRINKS BREAK. The first of the day. An hour where you might feel nothing has happened looking at the scorecard - 42/0 in 18.2 overs. But New Zealand have bowled really well and eked out plenty of inside edges. But none have resulted in wickets. The deficit is now just 64 and another good hour should make this Test look pretty good for the visitors. The pitch is starting to show some inconsistent bounce now, so batting will get difficult. Which means - first innings lead will be very crucial.

Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Full ball on middle and off, Pope drives this one beautifully down the ground. The ball hits the stumps at the non-striker's end. Mitchell tries to get his hand to it but fails to do so. The ball deflects off the stumps towards mid on.
On the hips, worked towards square leg for a single.
Another good area, just outside off, Pope walks across his stumps and pushes it towards gully.
Nice line, around off, angling away, but Pope is determined not to fiddle with those.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Around off, on a length, dabbed to third man, fine of wide slip, for a single.
INSIDE EDGE, MISSES THE STUMPS! 'C'mon!' yells Wagner in frustration. Full and outside off, Root looks to defend but gets an inside edge. The ball hits his left boot and rolls past the leg stump!
Outside off, pushed straight to point.

While we are talking about patience, let us now talk about discipline. The Kiwi bowlers have been disciplined so far but England need their batsmen to follow that principle as well. True, no wickets have fallen but there have been too many inside edges. A change in the field now. Ross Taylor goes to third man while Tom Latham swaps his position at short cover to point, with another Kiwi fielder.
Full and just outside off, solidly defended towards cover.
Half volley outside off, Ollie stays leg side of the ball and drives it towards mid off.

It is all a game of patience today. The surface looks a pretty hard one but it is also slowing up. So, timing would be tested and it could be one of those pitches where if you get one wicket, a couple more could follow quickly.
Full and around off again, Pope lunges to block.
Around off, blocked solidly.
Around off, coming in, defended to the leg side.
Full and around off, swinging away, watchfully defended down the pitch.
Full and outside off, Root looks drive but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Full and outside off, Ollie reaches out and pushes it towards point for a run.
Around off, left alone.
Outside off, pretty full and wide, Pope pushes at it but misses.
Full and outside off, Root looks to push but the ball squirts off the inside edge through mid-wicket. A single taken.
Neil Wagner changes ends. 26-3-85-1 so far. This is the end which has seen cracks open up and offer indifferent bounce.
Landed outside off, OP lets it through watchfully.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

BOTTOM EDGE, FOUR! Ahhh... Pope and his luck with the edges. Full and outside off, Ollie looks to push away from his body but there is no feet movement. The ball takes the bottom edge and goes past the off stump, past the diving Watling, to his left and into the fine leg fence. The deficit is now 68.
Full and around middle, almost a yorker, bunted down the ground, past the bowler. Mid on mops it up.
Around middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.

Another bowling change. Daryl Mitchell comes on. 12-4-28-0 so far. Ian Smith observes a substitute coming in with some drinks. He says that we have barely had 13 overs of play and substitutes are already on. With a scheduled Drinks Break, Smith wants players to control their urge to drink and quench their thirst. Professionalism.
Tossed up around off, well defended.
Walks into the shot now and pushes this towards mid on.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Full and wide outside off, good bowling, Pope reaches out and pushes it with hard hands towards point. Santner will like that. There is a possibility of an outside edge if Pope keeps doing that.
Around middle, pushed straight to cover.
Full and around middle, Root goes and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Spin for the first time this morning. Mitchell Santner is on. 17-4-32-0 so far. We can expect quite a long spell from him, if New Zealand cannot get wickets.
Landed outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Full and outside off, Pope looks to drive but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat down the ground.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a run.
A streaky way to get 300 on the scoreboard. Trail by 75 now. Full and around off, angling away, Pope stretches out to drive but the ball takes the inside edge and goes to fine leg. A single taken.
Full and outside off, angling further away, left alone.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Full and outside off, Root gets a big stride forward and blocks.
Around off, watchfully dabbed to wide slip.

FOUR! Uppish but safe! Williamson's innovative field placement nearly got him a wicket. A length ball outside off, Root looks to pull but the ball keeps a touch low. He plays the shot but it goes uppishly. Now, Williamson has stationed Ross Taylor at a squarish mid-wicket position. Not at the single-saving position, nor at the boundary. Somewhere in between. But it goes well wide of him, to his left and finds the fence. The skipper moves to 133. The deficit is also 76.
Full and just outside off, watchfully pushed towards mid on.
Excellent stop by Latham! Full and outside off, Pope leans and drives it through the covers but Tom at short extra cover dives full fledged to his left to stop the ball.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Another bouncer, pulled away by Root towards square leg for one.
FOUR! Plays that one very late! Bouncer just outside off, Root stays deep in his crease and upper cuts this one over the keeper's head. The ball races away to the fence.
Again Root goes to play this one in the gap between first slip and gully. However, it goes straight in the hands of the man at wide first slip on the bounce.
On the pads, Pope works this one towards square leg for a single.
On middle and off, Root goes back and pushes this one towards the left of the bowler.
Root this time safely defends it towards the off side.

FOUR! This time it is in the gap. Length ball outside off, Root opens the face of the bat and guides this one in the gap between wide first slip and gully. The ball races away to the third man fence. The man at gully did put in a full-stretch dive to his left but he still could not get to it.
On off, Root guides this with an angled bat softly towards the man at gully.
Again Root goes deep in his crease and blocks it out.
Length ball on middle and off, Root defends it back towards the bowler.
Ollie rocks onto the back foot and defends this one towards mid on.
Pitched up ball on off, pushed towards cover.
Bouncer on middle and off, it is slow. Root comfortably swivels across and pulls this behind square for a single.
Length ball angling into the batter, Root looks to push this one towards the off side but the ball goes off the inner half towards mid on.
Another ball which is pitched up, defended towards the off side.
Fullish ball on off, defended out.
Neil Wagner is into the attack for the first time in the day. 23-3-76-1, his figures so far.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Another bouncer, successfully ducked under.
Neil Wagner is warming up. Looks like he will be coming on to bowl soon.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
A short ball, around middle and leg, Pope initially looks to hook but then bails out. The ball keeps on climbing and Watling does excellently to dive to his left to gather.
Full and around off, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
On a length around off, defended down the ground.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Length ball outside off, punched towards the point region.
Full ball on off, driven towards mid off.

Beaten! Did that one pitch on a crack? Henry bowls a good length ball around off, the ball comes in after pitching. It shoots off the pitch. Pope looks to play at it but the ball whizzes past the outside edge. When the ball pitched, a puff of dust came out. Santner will like that!
On off again, Root guides this one towards the point region and takes a single.
Length ball just outside off, guided towards the man at gully.

A stifled appeal but nothing doing for the umpire. Southee bowls a length ball just outside off and gets it to nip back in. Pope gets back to defend but misses and is hit on the thigh pad. The Kiwi players appeal but the umpire shakes his head.
Fullish on off, pushed towards cover.
Pope gets right behind the line of the delivery and defends it.
Length ball on middle and off, Pope looks to defend but misses. It hits the thigh pad and rolls towards the slip cordon.
Length ball this time, outside off, Pope gets closer to the ball and defends it back towards the bowler.
Good length ball just outside off, defended towards the leg side.
Around off, coming in, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
Around off, defended from the crease.
Full and outside off, a touch wide, left alone.
Fractionally short in length outside off, Pope punches it through the covers but straight to the fielder.
A length ball outside off, punched to sweeper cover for a single.
Around off, curving away, punched towards cover.
Ohh! Beaten! This time it is Pope. Good length ball on off, it nips back in. Pope looks to defend but does so outside the line and is beaten. The ball whizzes past the inside edge.
Pope goes back in his crease and defends this one.
Length ball just outside off, Root punches this one towards cover-point and takes a single.
FOUR BYES! Down the leg side, Root goes for the flick but misses. Watling dives to his left but even he cannot get to the ball and the ball rolls into the fine leg fence for four byes.

Woah! That has stayed incredibly low! Southee bowls a good length ball just outside off, it pitches and stays very low. Root tries to bring his bat down and defend but he misses the ball completely. Had that ball been on the stumps, Root would have been a goner. The ball might have pitched on one of the cracks that might have opened up.
Good length ball just outside off, defended off the front foot towards mid off.
Pope again goes onto the back foot and punches this one towards cover.
The batsman has punched that ball through the offside.
Fullish on off this time, Pope drives this one towards cover.
Length ball on off, defended off the back foot towards the bowler.
Back of a length ball on middle, Pope plays a soft pull shot. It goes over the man at mid-wicket and the batters take two.
Fullish ball on middle and leg, driven towards wide mid on.
On the pads, flicked towards square leg for a single.
Length ball on off, it nips away a bit. Pope plays at it with soft hands but the ball goes off the outside edge towards the gully fielder. He dives to his right and holds onto it.
Some movement on this fuller ball for Southee, Pope drives this one towards mid off.
On the fourth stump line, Pope shuffles across a touch and defends this one off the back foot towards mid off.
Way wide outside off, Pope does not need to fiddle with it.
Southee serves a length ball outside off, Root plays this one towards point and takes a single.
Tim Southee it will be to bowl from the other end. 26-3-63-2 so far.
Length ball outside off, Ollie Pope makes a leave to get through the over.
Henry starts with a length ball in the corridor just outside off, Pope guides this one down towards third man and takes a couple. England underway on Day 4.
The players are out in the middle. The overnight batsmen, Joe Root and Ollie Pope, walk out to the middle. Matt Henry to complete his pending over. Pope to face.

Pitch report - Mark Richardson is down for the pitch report. Says that the weather conditions are overcast. The cracks have opened up a bit more than yesterday but they still won't have much affect on the match.

Good morning ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Day 4 of the second Test match between New Zealand and England. After a wait of almost 9 months, has English skipper Joe Root got his team back into the contest by scoring a ton? With the weather looking pretty bleak for Day 5, one would assume that the visitors have done enough as they trail the Kiwis by 106 runs. After being under the pump for the first 2 days, England applied themselves really well on Day 3 as Rory Burns and Joe Root both got to their respective tons. The Kiwis made a mini-comeback in the third session by taking 3 wickets and pushing England on the back foot again. With half the English side back in the hut and a new man at the crease, can the Kiwis enforce a collapse? All the updates coming up!
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

So, that will be it from Day 3. Rain has cut short the play on 2 out of the 3 days but we will be hoping that we get 2 uninterrupted days of play from here on in. Do join us at 1030 local (2130 GMT, Previous day) as there will be half an hour early start again to make up for the lost overs. You can now switch over to catch all the updates from the Adelaide Test where Pakistan are under the pump. Cheers!

In the third session, the Kiwi bowlers came back strongly rather than getting petered out. First they got rid of the dangerous Ben Stokes and then debutant Zak Crawley also followed him soon. The thorn for New Zealand heading into Day 4 will be the English skipper who is still at the crease and will be looking to get his team as close as he can to the hosts' total (trailing by 106 runs).

Yet another absorbing day of Test cricket! After seeing New Zealand's dominance on the first two days, the picture changed on Day 3. England made a roaring comeback through the partnership between Joe Root and Rory Burns. The pair saw off the entire morning session safely and then followed the same for most parts of the afternoon as well. They raised a 177-run stand and Burns notched up his century before getting run out towards the end of the second session.
Play has been ABANDONED for the day! With all the rain around, it was next to impossible to get the ground ready by 1800 local. So that will be it. Stumps on Day 3!

Auskar - Wow. Just got up from sleep, switched on the TV and bang, bang! Stokes gone, Crawley gone. I must be lucky for NZ. @Auskar - 'Interesting observation. How about changing your sleeping patterns for the next 2 days?'
Outside off, left alone by Ollie.
Good length ball on off, pushed back towards the bowler.

Update 1732 local - It has started to drizzle. The intensity is increasing and the umpires have decided to take the players off the park. The covers are on to protect the playing area. More covers are coming now. Stay tuned for more updates...
Bad fielding by Santner again! Outside off, Pope drives at this one and the ball goes towards cover where Santner is positioned. He misfields and that allows the batters to take a couple.
Length ball on middle and off, blocked out.
Matt Henry is back into the attack. 21-5-54-1, his figures so far.
Way outside the off stump, Joe lets it go.
Oh dear! Movement near the boundary line. Groundsmen are getting the covers ready. They seem to be anticipating some rain.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Play and a miss! A good length ball on middle and leg, angling away from Root. He looks to have a poke at it but misses and the ball whizzes past the outside edge. Root looks really unhappy with the fading light and shares some quiet words with the square leg umpire.
Fullish ball outside off, pushed towards the man at cover.
Good length ball outside off, Root makes another leave.
Length ball wide outside off, left alone.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended back towards the bowler.
Another one outside off, Pope shoulders arms.
The artificial lights are switched on as it has turned gloomy out there.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
On the pads, Pope works this one towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length ball on off, Root swivels and pulls this one behind square leg for a single.
Full ball, almost a yorker on the off pole. Root jams it out back towards the bowler.

DRINKS! So, after two sessions completely dominated by the Englishmen, the Kiwis have staged half a comeback by sending Stokes and debutant Crawley back to the pavilion. The Kiwis still possess a lead of 109 runs but with Root still out in the middle, it is in danger of being extinguished. The New Zealand bowlers need to keep on doing the good work and pile on the pressure on the lower order batters now with Root looking well set.
Length ball on the hips, pushed down the ground towards mid on.
Outside off, angling away from Pope. He does not fiddle with it.
Another length ball around off, pushed towards extra cover.
Good length delivery on middle and off, blocked out.
Length ball wide outside off, left alone.
Full ball on off, Root pushes this one down the ground and sets off. Williamson from mid off runs across to his right and has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. Single taken.
Angles in a length ball on off, Pope sticks back and defends it right under his eyes.
Ollie has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Looks to drive it off his front foot but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Good length ball on middle, Root defends it from the crease to the on side.
Hint of away movement outside off, Root shoulders arms.
Too straight in line and Pope eases it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Edgy! A length delivery in the area around middle and leg, Pope is squared up in defense and it takes the leading edge before rolling back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Oohhh... this one stays low! Wagner angles across a good length ball outside off, Pope pushes at it but it goes under his bat.
Ollie Pope is the new batsman.

OUT! Caught behind! Crawley's 6-ball stay in the middle is over. Wagner comes up with a pinpoint delivery in the region around middle and off, Crawley goes nowhere with his footwork and has a tame push inside the line. It skids on with the angle, takes a faint outside edge and Watling completes the catch with a dive to his right. England trail by 113 runs with half their side back in the hut!
Fullish and outside off, driven through covers for a single.
On the pads and Root has worked it behind square leg for a single.

NOT OUT! Crawley has dived his way to safety! A length ball around off, Zak drives it to mid off and sets off for a quick run. Kane Williamson attacks the ball and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end as Crawley dives in. The Kiwis are celebrating and it's referred upstairs. The replays confirm that the dive has saved the young man and he is off the mark in Test cricket. Will always remember his first!
Direct hit! New Zealand are celebrating. Has the dive saved Crawley? It's referred upstairs and the replays find Zak to be safe. He is off the mark in Test career in the most nervous way.
Full and angling in on middle, Crawley knocks it down to mid on where the fielder stops it well.
Edged but safe! Crawley is showing nerves. Southee delivers a ball moving away from the batsman, Crawley pushes inside the line and gets a soft outside edge wide of gully.
Crawley lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Short in length around off, Root pulls it through square leg for one.
Digs it in on middle, Root pulls it down to fine leg for a run.
FOUR! Width on offer outside off, Root latches onto it and smashes it over backward point for a boundary. All the pressure is gone and we can now see a free-flowing Joe!
Good length ball outside off, Root taps it down to covers.

FOUR! Root reaches his 17th Test hundred in a rather unconvincing way. The wait of 9 months is over. It's a long wait given the caliber of this batsman. He has been under the scanner for his dipping form and this knock has come at the best possible time. He reached there in an ugly manner though. Shortish ball close to off, Root is cramped for room as he tries to play the square cut. It catches the bottom edge and bounces over the leaping keeper for a boundary. Root is a relieved man. But his job is not done yet. England are still trailing by over 100 runs.
FOUR! Easy pickings! A length ball sliding down the leg side, Root deflects it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Outside off, played down off the back foot to point.
Defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Zack Crawley, the debutant, walks out to bat now.

OUT! Fine low catch by Ross Taylor at first slip! Southee produces a brilliant delivery from 'round the wicket. He angles it in around off and gets it to nip away a shade. Stokes reaches out for it with firm hands and gets a thick outside edge behind. Taylor dives across to his right to snap it safely. Stokes looks behind and after seeing Rosco claiming the catch and celebrating, he returns to the pavilion.
EDGED! But has that carried? Ross Taylor is claiming the catch and Ben Stokes takes his word. He is walking back.
Too full in length and outside off, Stokes taps it down with soft hands to the off side.
This time Stokes leans into the drive and pushes it to covers.
On a length and close to off, Stokes blocks it off his back foot.
Good length delivery in the corridor outside off, Stokes picks the line early and makes a leave.
Joe Root puts some drying spray on his hands. Seems he is feeling the heat of the 90s and has sweaty palms.
Closer to off on a good length, Root defends it solidly to the off side.
Switches to 'round the wicket and hurls in a good length ball outside off, Joe allows it through to the keeper.
On a length around off, Root stays back and defends it towards cover-point.
Full in length and on middle, Stokes uses the angle and clips it behind square leg for a run.
Ufff! This one stays low and goes underground! Wagner delivers it on a length close to off, Stokes tries to defend but it goes under his bat and misses the off pole by a whisker.
In the zone outside off, Stokes covers his stumps and shoulders arms. There was a hint of away shape!
A length ball on off, Joe stays back and pushes it towards wide mid off.
FOUR! Off the thickish outside edge! Fullish ball outside off, Root tries to drive it with an angled bat but it takes the outer half and hurries past the diving gully fielder for a boundary.
Yorker outside off, Stokes squeezes it out square of the wicket on the off side for a single.
Lands it full and close to off, Stokes drives it off the outer portion of his bat to mid off.
Short in length and outside off, Stokes shoulders arms.
Full in length on off, moving back in, Stokes forces it down to mid on.
Bowling change. Tim Southee is back into the attack. His figures so far read 21-2-53-1.
Wagner goes very full and on middle, Root gets his bat down in time as he digs it out.

A mishit! Width on offer outside off, Root chases it and throws his bat. It catches the bottom edge and goes behind. Watling dives across to his right and the first slip fielder collects the ball on one bounce.

FOUR! And this boundary takes him into the 90s! Wagner pitches it up around off and Root stylishly leans into the cover drive. He middles his shot beautifully and sends it screaming away to the fence.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks it solidly from the back foot.
Fuller length ball angling in on middle, Root punches it down the ground and it goes over the bowler. The mid off fielder gets across to his right to stop the ball.
Just 8 overs and the second new ball has lost its shape. Very poor quality. The reserve umpire comes out with a box of balls.
Uses the angle of the bowler and helps the length ball to mid-wicket.
Fuller in length and outside off, driven solidly off the front foot to mid off.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Sublime! Back of a length ball on off, Stokes camps back and punches it sweetly past the left side of the diving cover fielder. The mid off fielder chases but comes second best.
A length ball around off, Stokes meets it with the full face of his bat and eases it past the bowler to mid off.
Fractionally short and moving back into the batsman from around middle, Stokes pushes it firmly to mid on.
Fullish and outside off, pushed off the front foot to covers.
Root shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On a length and outside off, Root keeps his weight on the back foot and allows it through the line.

Hammer time! One of the groundsmen is charging to the middle. He uses the hammer to level the surface near the bowler's landing area. Now Wagner takes the matter, or rather the hammer into his own hands and he too is leveling the surface near the landing area. 'Is he qualified to do that? ...quips the on-air commentator!'
This one straightens nicely. Fullish and on middle, Root is opened up slightly in his defense and he keeps it out off the outer half of his blade.
Good length ball angling away from the batsman, wide outside off, Joe shoulders arms.

A cracking yorker on middle at 124.5 kph, Root keeps his eyes glued to the ball and digs it out down to mid on. As the innings has progressed, Joe has become a lot better with his transfer of weight into the shot. Initially Root was seen reaching out for the ball by leaning forward and now he is trying to play right under his watchful eyes.
Neil Wagner has been unleashed into the attack. 16-1-54-0, his figures so far. Can Wagner produce some magic with the second new ball?
Henry sends an invitation for a drive outside off, Stokes declines the offer.

Uppish but safe! A length ball on middle and leg, angling down, Stokes turns to work it on the leg side but closes the face of the bat early. It pops out off the leading edge but doesn't carry to mid on.
Very full in length and around leg, it's clipped behind square leg for a single.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Offers the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
FOUR! Slapped away! Short of a length delivery wide outside off, Stokes gets on top of the bounce and whacks it behind square on the off side. It flies over the gully fielder for a boundary.
Good length ball on off, Stokes is on the back foot in defense.
Fuller length ball around off, angling in, Stokes shows the full face of his bat as he tries to play it straight. It comes slightly off the inner half and squirts to mid off.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Absolutely delightfully! Southee is very full and wide outside off, Stokes accepts the proposal of driving it through the line and creams it through the gap at covers.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
A back foot punch this time by Root but he finds the cover fielder.
Henry puts it on a length and close to off, angling in, Root defends it stoutly to the off side.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A length ball outside off, Root stays back and pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Goes full and angles it on middle, Root flicks it across the line but finds the mid-wicket fielder.

Almost a drag on! Henry dishes out a good length ball close to off and it holds its line upon landing, Root gets back inside the crease to punch it through the line but it takes the inside edge and strikes him on the right leg.
Hurls a gentle delivery in the zone wide outside off, Stokes is in no mood to chase it.
Slants in a length ball on off, Stokes remains back and pushes it to mid on.
Pitches it up and outside off, Stokes plays a free-flowing cover drive but finds the fielder.
Angles in a full length ball on off, Stokes covers the line and blocks it off his front foot.
Lands it on a length and outside off, Ben shoulders arms with ease.
Fullish and on the pads, clipped to square leg for one.
Tim Southee to continue...

Fantastic effort by Wagner! An overpitched delivery on middle, Stokes whips it past mid on and Wagner gives the chase. He dives near the fence to keep it inside the line and saves two runs for his team. Great commitment.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, Stokes covers the line and shoulders arms.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Henry switches to 'round the wicket and spears in a full ball on off, Stokes meets it with a straight bat and pushes it off the inner half to mid on.
Again the length is very full around middle, angling in, Root eases it wide of mid on and crosses for a single.
Right on the money first up! Almost a yorker on off, Root brings his bat down in time and pushes it towards mid on.

We're back for the last session. It's going to be a vital phase of this Test match as the second new ball has been taken and the conditions are overcast. New Zealand would be hoping to take advantage of that! 35 overs are left in the day. Matt Henry (17-4-46-1) to run in first up...
... DAY 3, FINAL SESSION ...

76/1 in 28 overs - Another good session for England, just losing the centurion Rory Burns. The pair of Joe Root and Burns batted fluently in the afternoon and played some superb shots. They extended their partnership beyond the 150-run mark and also brought the deficit under 200. An error in judging the second run cost Rory his wicket and the Black Caps finally got the breakthrough they dearly needed since the start of Day 3. The second new ball has been taken and with the cloud cover and a new batsman in the middle, New Zealand would be hoping to make further inroads in the last session. Do join us at 1600 local (0300 GMT) for more action.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Stokes to get through the second session of the day. That will be TEA ON DAY 3.
Fullish ball just outside the off pole line, Stokes looks to defend but the ball goes off the outer half of the bat towards point for a couple.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good length ball on middle and off, Stokes defended it out.
Way too wide outside off, Stokes shoulders arms.
Some swing straightaway with the new ball. Southee comes from around the wicket and releases this one from way outside the off pole, it tails back in a lot but just not enough to trouble the batter.
SECOND NEW BALL IS AVAILABLE! New Zealand waste no time and take it straightaway. One more over left in the session. Tim Southee returns to bowl it. It's turning overcast now.
Floated on middle and off, Root prods forward and defends.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Santner bowls a floated ball outside off, left alone by Root.
Root goes back deep in his crease and defends.
Another one which is dragged back, Stokes goes onto the back foot and pushes it towards the cover region. The fielder there dives and makes a good half-stop but the batters take a single.
Santner bowls a shortish ball on middle, Stokes pushes it down to mid on.
Mitchell Santner comes back on. 16-4-31-0, his figures so far.
Full ball on off, driven towards the cover region.
On middle and leg, defended by Root.
Again on off, pushed towards the off side.
Very full ball on off, Root superbly drives it towards cover but straight to the man.
On the off side, Root opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man.
Length ball outside off, played towards point.
Full ball on off, blocked out towards the off side.
On the pads, flicked towards mid-wicket.
Again Stokes drives it down the ground but this time straight to the man at mid off.
FOUR! Brilliant, absolutely brilliant! Overpitched ball on the off pole line, Stokes has driven this one with class through mid on for a boundary.
On the pads of Stokes, he works this one towards the leg side.
Good length ball on the off pole line by Wagner, bowling with a scrambled seam. Stokes shuffles across and works this one towards square leg for a couple.
Outside off, length ball. Root leaves it alone.
Full ball around off, Root shuffles and drives this one down the ground. The man from mid on runs across and stops it.
This time it is on off, driven towards extra cover.
On the pads, driven towards mid on.
Pitched up ball just outside off, Root defends with a vertical bat.
Full ball on middle, defended out.
Length ball wide outside off, played towards point.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
On off, driven superbly towards the cover region.
On the pads of Root, he works it towards square leg for a single. Santner there picks up the ball and has a shy at the striker's end and hits. However, Stokes is well in.
Way outside the off pole, Root shoulders arms.
FOUR! Great shot by Root. Good length ball outside off, Root opens the face of his bat and guides this one between gully and backward point towards the third man fence.

The reserve umpire has come out and changed the bails. The earlier ones in use were white in colour and it was quite tough for the third umpire to find out whether they were dislodged in the white background (Watling's jersey colour when he was breaking the stumps to dismiss Rory Burns). Bails of woody colour in place now. Well done! It's all about correcting mistakes and being proactive.
A gentle delivery in the channel outside off, Stokes lifts his bat skywards and allows it through.
Leans forward to a full ball and pushes it gently to short cover.
Closer to the off stump this time, on a length, Stokes middles his defensive shot and pushes it to mid off.
Action replay of the previous delivery. Ben has been quite watchful at the moment.
Pitches it up and outside off, Stokes strides forward and shoulders arms.
Lands it on a length and outside off, Root drives it through cover-point for a single.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. Successful over at last for the Kiwis!
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
High full toss down the leg side, Stokes flicks this one towards the fine leg region and takes a single to get off the mark. Interestingly, it's not called a no ball.
Ben Stokes is the new batsman with England trailing by 174 runs.

OUT! RUN OUT! Burns has thrown his wicket away just after getting to his ton. He will be fuming with himself right now. Wagner bowls this one the pads of Burns, he flicks this one towards mid-wicket and sets off for a single. Root calls Burns for the second and he obliges. Raval from deep mid-wicket runs in and throws it at the striker's end. Watling dislodges the bails and appeals. The umpire refers it upstairs. After numerous replays and various angles, the third umpire gives it out. Bruce Oxenford used all possible frames there to make his decision. Also, the colour of bails were white and to pick whether they were dislodged from the white background (Watling's jersey colour) was quite a challenge. Eventually, the right decision has been made and that's paramount. Even after scoring a ton, Burns walks out of the park looking like a disappointed man and rightly so. However, he has played a handy role in reviving his team's fortune.

Run out appeal! Rory Burns is the batsman under the scanner. It seems to be touch and go in the replays. The third umpire watches it from multiple angles and takes his own sweet time. Eventually Rory is found inches short of the crease in one frame.
Back of a length ball on the leg side, Root pulls this one towards mid-wicket and takes a single.

Here it is... SECOND TEST CENTURY FOR RORY BURNS! He has been given three lives and has made sure to make the most of it and put the Kiwis under the pump. On the pads of Rory, he flicks this one towards fine leg and takes a single to get to his ton. He removes his helmet and enjoys the ovation from the dressing room. The England opener will now be looking to convert this into a daddy hundred!
Another one outside off, this time Burns pushes it towards cover off the back foot and takes a single to move to 99. He retains strike for the next over.
FOUR! Punched away! Length ball wide outside off, Burns makes room and punches this one towards point for a boundary.
This time Root pierces the gap at cover inside the circle. The ball goes to the man at sweeper cover and that allows the batters to take one.
Good length ball on off, pushed towards cover.
Full ball on off, driven towards the cover region.
Good length ball outside off, Root opens the face of the bat and guides this one towards short third man.
Slower yorker by Wagner on off, at 112 kph. Burns does well to keep it out.
Full ball on off, driven towards mid off.
Wagner attacks the stumps now. Burns brings his bat down in time and the ball goes off the inner half towards mid on.
Burns in two minds here! Wagner bowls this one on a length just outside off, the ball moves away from the batter. Burns initially looks to play at it but eventually pulls his bat away.
Good running by the English batters. Root goes deep in his crease and pushes this length ball wide of mid on. Burns trusts his partner and sets off straightaway to complete an easy single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Good length ball in the corridor outside off, Burns pushes this one towards point. Maiden to start off his new spell.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Burns drives this pitched up ball towards mid off.
Another one outside off, Burns shoulders arms to let that one through.
Now Mitchell goes fuller, Burns pushes this one towards mid off.
Mitchell start with a length ball outside off, Burns leaves it alone.
Daryl Mitchell is back on. 7-1-21-0, his figures so far. Can the local lad come up with something that can dislodge this high-flying batting pair?
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Slower again, full and dipping into the batsman, Burns flicks it wide of mid on for a run.
Play and a miss! Width on offer outside off, Burns flashes and misses. Getting nervous in the 90s?
Zippy delivery on this occasion. Wagner bowls it outside off and it skids through the surface after pitching. Burns guards his stumps and shoulders arms.
Beaten completely! A knuckle ball by Wagner. It's very full and outside off, gripping and cutting away upon landing, Burns tries to force it away on the off side but is beaten.
Fuller in length and outside off, Burns drives it off his front foot to mid off.
Too full in length and outside off, Root mistimes his drive to covers.
Interesting! Flatter and a touch shorter outside off, Root shuffles across the stumps and then defends close to his pads. There was some extra bounce and Joe somehow managed to keep it out to safely.
No attacking fielder other than a slip now. Short leg has vanished and there is a deep square leg in place.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot.
FOUR! Superb shot! Loopy full ball around off, Root kneels and nails his sweep shot in front of square leg for a powerful boundary. England are in command!
Flighted and full on middle, Joe leans forward and defends.
Tossed up ball outside off, Root has nothing to do with it.

Drinks break. Another hour of play safely negotiated by the pair of Joe Root and Rory Burns. They continue to be in full control of their game and have extended their partnership to 162 runs. The deficit has also come under 200 and New Zealand will be feeling the heat at the moment. They did get the chance to run out Rory Burns but failed to take it and now the southpaw has three lives en route 93. He will be looking for his century and inflict more damage on the Kiwis.
On the pads, Root works this one towards the leg side and takes a single.
Outside off, Root plays it with an angled bat towards gully.
Again Root pushes at a length and again he gets a thick outside edge on it. This time the man at wide first slip takes it on the bounce.

EDGED AND FOUR! Root is a lucky man! Good length ball outside off, it pitches and nips away from the batter. Root pushes at it with soft hands but the ball goes off the outside edge through the gap between wide first slip and the keeper through to the third man fence.
Length ball on middle and off, Root goes deep in his crease and defends.
Full ball wide outside off, Root jams it out towards point.
Burns has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up ball on off, swept away through square leg for one.
Bowling change. Neil Wagner is back into the attack. 10-1-31-0, his figures so far. Can he provide the all-important breakthrough for the Kiwis?
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR LEG BYES! Whoa! This one turns square. Santner serves a flatter delivery on middle and it spins away after landing. Root is opened up in his stance as he tries to work it away. Fails to put bat on ball and is hit on the flap of the back pad. The bowler appeals but doesn't receive support from the keeper. It has hurried behind for a boundary at third man. The replays find the impact to be comfortably outside off.
Root has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flighted and outside off, left alone.
A pitched up ball outside off has been driven through the line but straight to covers.

FOUR! Easily done! Burns enters into the 90s! Short in length and around off, it nicely sits up for the batsman. Burns rides the bounce and pulls it handsomely to the deep mid-wicket fence. 150-run stand comes up as well! The deficit is under 200 now!
In the channel outside off, another leave made by Rory.
Outside off, left alone.
Full in length on middle and off, driven back to the bowler and Henry made a fine diving stop to his left.
Knocks a full ball down the ground towards mid on.
Short and outside off, cut through point for one.
Root has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.
Turns it off his pads to the leg side, finds the gap and takes a run.
Rory has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.

Run out chance missed! Burns survives. What was Henry thinking there? Fullish ball around off, Burns uses his wrists to flick it through mid-wicket and eyes the second run. He is sent back by Root and Rory charges back. But before that, the fielder (Wagner) from the deep has released his throw and it's in the direction of the stumps at the non-striker's end. But Henry tries to collect it ahead of the wickets and fumbles. That gives Burns the chance to dive back in safely. Latham was perfectly stationed behind the sticks and had Matt not intervened, Burns would have been found short. Big miss!
Fuller length ball on middle, Root picks it off his pads and clips it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Fuller in length and close to off, Burns works it on the leg side, in front of square leg, and jogs across for a single.
In the region outside off, angling away, Rory shoulders arms.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Quicker and flatter on off, defended off the back foot.
Another good looking drive from the bat of Root but he finds the cover fielder.

FOUR! Beautiful timing and placement! Loopy delivery landing full and outside off, Root leans into the square drive and caresses it through the gap. The cover-point fielder gives the chase but it goes away spinning from him and he eventually fails to pull it back in play.
Flatter and on middle, Root hangs on the back foot and helps it on the leg side.
Floated and full on middle, Joe strides forward and defends it back.
Skidding down the leg side, Root fails to flick and it goes off his pads to fine leg. They take a couple of leg byes.
Another easy leave outside the off stump to complete an innocuous over.
Outside off, left alone.
Full in length close to off, angling away again, Burns parks his front foot forward and across before shouldering arms.
On a length and outside off, Burns strides forward and pushes it to mid off.
Good length ball in the channel outside off, leaving the left-hander with the angle, Burns shoulders arms.
Back of a length ball on middle and leg, Root nudges it towards fine leg and picks up a single. Given as a leg bye.
Matt Henry replaces Southee into the attack. 14-3-38-1, his figures so far.
Goes down on one knee and sweeps a full ball from the off stump line. He sends it to deep square leg and retains strike with a single.
Quicker through the air this time, it's flat and on the pads, Root moves back and taps it down to short leg.
An arm ball around off, Root prods forward and defends it ahead of his front pad.
Extra flight there, it lands full and wide outside off, Root cracks his drive off the front foot but finds the cover fielder.
Full and floated outside off, Root covers the line and leaves it alone.
Flatter and a touch shorter on off, Root goes on the back foot in defense.
Lets the ball go outside his off stump. Another over safely negotiated! Just wearing down the Kiwi bowlers.
Pitches it up and around off, Burns drives it off his front foot to short cover.
Slower delivery, full and wide outside off, Rory takes a stride forward and then allows it through.
FOUR! Crunched! Short in length and around off, Burns stands tall inside the crease and pulls it with authority to the deep mid-wicket fence. That's raced away.
Full in length and outside off, Burns drives it on the up but finds the wide mid off fielder.
Angling away from the left-hander, outside off. Burns keeps his bat close to his body as he makes a leave.

Mishit! Good bowling by Santner. This time he manages to lure the batsman into a drive by giving it some extra air. Burns throws his bat at it and slices it down to deep point for a single. Not where he intended to play that shot.
Continues to toss them up! Full and on off, this time it's blocked with the spin to mid-wicket.
Nicely flighted by Santner and he lands it very full on off, Rory leans forward and defends it.
Loopy delivery outside off, turning in a bit, Burns gets back and has enough time to play it towards mid-wicket.
Bowls this one with a round-arm action, around leg, Root gets back and tucks it to fine leg for one. Just too easy to rotate the strike for these two.
Tossed up ball landing full on middle, Root lunges and defends it to short leg.
Fullish and on off, pushed off the front foot to mid off. End of the over and it continues to be easy going for England.
Pitches it up and outside off, angling away, Rory allows it through comfortably.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Southee appears to be working on a plan to lure Burns into a drive and eke out an outside edge. This time though he serves it way wide outside off, Rory has nothing to do with it.
Length ball outside off, Root goes back and cuts this one towards backward point for one. This single brings up 150 runs for England. They trail by 225 runs.
Outside off, played towards point.
This time flatter by Santner, Burns goes deep in his crease and works this one towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up delivery on off, turning back in. Burns goes back and defends.
Shortish outside off, Root rocks back and cuts this one towards backward point for one.
Flatter outside off, Burns shuffles and works this one towards the leg side for a single.
Leg side field is strengthened. Clearly aiming at Rory Burns' sweep shots.
Santner drags it short, Root goes deep in his crease and works this one towards square leg for a single.
Floated on off, Root prods forward and blocks.
A real tempter by Southee. He delivers it on the driving length and it's a slower one. Burns takes his front leg forward and then decides to make a leave.
A length ball close to off, Burns strides forward and defends it back solidly.
Once again it's overpitched by Southee on middle, Root stands on top of it as he flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Pitches it up and outside off, Burns leans into the drive and sends it through point for a run.
A touch short in length this time, wide outside off, Burns has nothing to do with it.
Good length ball on middle, Burns gets back to work it on the leg side but is late in closing the face of his bat. It takes the leading half and rolls to mid off.
Extra loop on this delivery, it's full and on off, Root strokes it by pressing forward but fails to beat the diving short cover fielder.
Too full in length and around off, driven back in the direction of the bowler.
Flighted one, full and on off, Root lunges and defends it to the off side.
Bowls this one with a quicker-arm action and lands it full around off, Burns goes down and sweeps it behind square leg for one.
Flatter this time, around off and on the shorter side, Burns goes on the back foot and blocks.
Flighted and full around off, Burns is on the front foot in defense.
Mitchell Santner to continue from this end post Lunch.
Full in length and wide outside off, Root leans into the drive and middles his shot well. Although he finds the cover fielder.
Nopes, that's a double bluff! Tim overpitches on middle, Burns does well to flick it through mid-wicket for a single.
Square leg drops back. Short stuff coming?
Southee gets closer to off stump, it's on a length and Burns defends it from the crease to short cover.
Lands it around off and takes it away with the angle, Burns sticks inside the crease and shoulders arms.
This one is further wide outside off, a very easy lave for Rory this time.
Southee begins his new spell with a fuller length delivery outside off, Burns takes his front leg forward to cover the line and then makes a leave.

Back for the afternoon session! The men concerned are slowly coming back on the field. Joe Root has finally found some runs to silence his critics for the time being and Rory Burns is making full use of the lives granted to him last evening. But the thing is that they cannot afford to relax. England would want them to repeat their morning session performance and take them as close as possible to 375. New Zealand will try to remain disciplined with their bowling and hope for some support from the pitch. Tim Southee (14-2-34-1) to kick off proceedings.
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

What a satisfactory morning for England! They were treading on thin ice at the close of play on Day 2 but the pair of Joe Root and Rory Burns applied themselves beautifully this morning and their century partnership has given the touring team breathing space. They are not out of jail yet as the deficit is over 200 and the current stand has to continue to bring them to safer shores. There is nothing on offer from the surface and the Black Caps will be ruing those dropped catches of Rory Burns. Both the English batsmen have scored their fifties and are looking determined for a big one. From where will the breakthrough come for New Zealand? Do join us at 1340 local (0040 GMT) to find out.

Flatter delivery outside off, it pitches and skids back in a bit. Root offers no stroke and is hit on the pads. The Kiwi players put in a stifled appeal but nothing doing for the umpire. Hasn't skidded back in enough. That will be LUNCH ON DAY 3.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up on off, Root defends by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Root prods forward and defends this one out.
On off this time, Root guides this one towards cover-point.
Tossed up on the pads, tucked towards the leg side.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Fullish ball on off, driven towards mid off.
Another one way outside off, Burns does not fiddle with it.
Outside off, left alone.

50 up for Joe Root! His 46th half century in Test cricket. On the pads of Root, he flicks this one towards mid-wicket for a single to get to his half ton. He is well set here and would be looking to take his side close to New Zealand's total first. Can the English skipper convert this start into a ton?
Good length ball on middle and off, defended out.
Floated on off, blocked out.
Tossed up on off, pushed towards mid on.
Root goes back deep in his crease and works this one behind square on the leg side for a single.
Another one floated on middle, tucked towards the leg side.
Floated on middle, defended out.
On the pads, worked away towards the leg side.
On the pads of Root, he flicks this one towards mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

NOT OUT! Good decision to review the umpire's call by Root. Good length ball down the leg side, Root looks to flick this one but fails to do so. The ball carries to BJ Watling behind the wickets who puts in a loud appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Root straightaway without consulting his partner signals the 'T'. Replays roll in, Hot Spot comes in and shows no bat involved. It shows that it has hit Root on the pad. Snicko confirms the same. Root survives and he will be looking to score big here.

Review time! Root has been adjudged caught behind but he has gone straightaway for the review. He seems very confident that there is no edge on it and the Hot Spot confirms it. Review successful and Root survives.
On the pads, flicked towards mid-wicket.
Length delivery on middle and leg, driven towards mid on.
Good length ball on off, defended by Root.
Daryl Mitchell is back into the attack. 5-1-19-0, his figures so far.

FOUR! Swept away! Burns has hardly missed a scoring opportunity in this innings. Tossed up delivery down the leg side, Burns gets down on one knee and sweeps this one fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Another one on the hips, Burns goes back and defends.
On the hips, tucked towards the man at square leg.
Floated on off, Root punches it towards mid off and takes a single.
Tossed up on off, Root defends it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Root plays this one towards the man at point.
Another fuller ball on off, this time Burns punches it down the ground through mid off and the batters take two as the fielder from mid off chases it and cuts it off.
Full ball wide outside off, Burns middles this one over the cover fielder. The man at sweeper cover cuts it off and the batters take a couple.
Yorker just outside off, jammed out towards mid off.
On the pads of Root, he flicks this one towards mid-wicket for a single.
Length ball on the pads, Burns punches this one towards mid-wicket. The bowler gives it a chase but cannot stop the single.
Very full ball on off, driven towards the man at silly mid off.
Another one outside off, Root gets down on one knee and punches it towards cover-point. Maiden!
Outside off, pushed towards the point region.
Tossed up on off, pushed towards cover.
Similar delivery, Root goes back and defends.
Flatter one just outside off, defended.
Floated delivery outside off, blocked out.
Length ball outside off, Burns shoulders arms.
Bowls this one very wide outside off, Burns does not fiddle with it.
Another good length ball outside off, left alone by the batter.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
On the pads, Root works this one towards mid-wicket and takes a single.
On off, Burns pushes it towards the cover region for a single.
Santner sprays one down the leg side, Root goes back and nudges it fine down the leg side for a couple.
Outside off, Root pushes this one towards the cover region.
Floated on middle and off, defended well by Root.
Root has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated on middle and off, Root defends it out.
Yorker on the pads, worked towards backward square leg by Burns for a run. This brings up the 100-run stand between Root and Burns, just what the doctor ordered for England.

Stifled appeal but nothing from the umpire. Length ball on middle and leg, Root looks to flick but misses. He is hit high on the pad and the Kiwi players put in a stifled appeal but nothing doing for the umpire.
Length delivery just outside off, Burns goes for the drive but instead slices it through point for a single.
In the corridor just outside off, Burns shoulders arms.
Pitched up on off, driven towards mid off.
FOUR! Driven beautifully! Identical delivery, this time Burns gets his timing right and the ball races through mid on and beats the diving attempt by the fielder there.

JUST SHORT! Henry bowls a full ball on off, inviting Burns to drive and he obliges. The ball takes the outside edge of Burns' bat and goes towards gully where Nicholls is positioned. However, the ball falls just short of him.
Floated on middle and off, Root defends it with a straight bat.
On off, played towards point.
Root prods forward and defends this one by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Again Santner gives this a lot of air on off, Root converts this into a full toss and drives this one towards cover. The man there makes a good diving stop.
Floated on off, defended towards the cover region.
Length ball on middle and leg, Burns goes back and defends.
On the pads, flicked towards mid-wicket.
Fuller delivery on off, Root punches this powerfully towards the cover region. The fielder there dives to his left, half-stops it and that allows the batters to take a single.
Good length ball just outside off, Root goes back and defends.
This time it is fullish by Henry, Root opens the face of the bat and guides it towards point.
Henry starts his new spell with a good length ball just outside off, Root defends it out.
Matt Henry (10-3-24-1) returns for another spell this morning as New Zealand continue their search for the first wicket on Day 3.
Santner floats this one just outside off, Burns comes onto the front foot and blocks it out.
Skidding back into the batsman from the arm of the bowler, it's around middle and leg, Root moves inside the crease and turns it wide of short leg for a single.
This time Root prods forward to this floated ball and punches it back towards the bowler.
Again Root goes onto the back foot and defends it out.
Shortish delivery by Santner. It is bowled outside off, Root goes back and plays this one towards point.
Floated delivery outside off, Burns gets down on one knee and sweeps this one through square leg for a single.
Fullish ball just outside off, Root blocks it out.
Outside off, Root pushes it towards point.
Good length ball on off, Burns prods forward and drives this one towards the cover region and takes a single.
Bangs it short around off and Root pulls it in front of square leg for a single.
Good length ball on off, Joe remains on the back foot and punches it in front of square on the off side.
Wagner continues to bowl from 'round the wicket to the right-hander. Delivers it on a length around off, Root drives it to covers with a hesitant front foot movement.
Burns defends it from within the crease.

Appeal for an LBW but turned down! Santner bowls a shortish ball outside off and gets it to spin back into the batsman. Burns looks to shuffle and defend this one towards the leg side. He fails to do so and is hit high on the pads. The Kiwi players put in a stifled appeal but nothing from the umpire. New Zealand opt not to take the review. Replays later show that there was an inside edge onto the pads.
On the pads, Burns works t away towards the leg side.
Drags one back this time, Burns goes back and defends.
Darts one outside off, Burns prods forward and blocks.
Starts with a ball right on the boot of Burns, he works this one towards square leg.

It's spin time! Mitchell Santner has been introduced into the attack. Wagner did get his slower ones to grip and move. Let's see how much assistance Santner gets here. A slip and short leg in place...
Fullish ball on leg, driven towards mid on.
On the pads of Burns, he looks to flick this one but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards the leg side and the batters steal a leg bye.

Variation from Wagner! Almost deceived Root with a beauty! Wagner steams in and bowls a knuckle ball from wide of the crease. It is a slow dipping yorker which swerves in the air. Root just about gets his bat down in time and the ball goes off the inner half of his bat towards fine leg for a single.
Good length ball on off, driven towards mid off.
Joe has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fullish and on off, Root drives it off his front foot to mid off.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Length ball on middle and off, defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! On the pads, Burns looks in much better touch now as he flicks this one nonchalantly through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Fullish on middle, driven towards mid on.

EDGED AND FOUR! Mitchell pitches one up on the off side, inviting Burns for the drive. Rory obliges as he brings out the straight driver but the ball goes off the outside edge between the wide first slip and gully fielders towards the third man region for a boundary.
Full ball on middle and leg to start off after the mini break, Root drives it down the ground and the mid on fielder slides to his left and keeps it down to a single.

Drinks break. Good show of intent by England in the first segment of the extended morning session. The current pair has pounced on every opportunity to score runs and has not allowed the Kiwi bowlers to build any pressure. Still, the tourists can ill afford to relax as there is plenty of work remaining.
Length ball on middle and off, Burns goes back in his crease and blocks it out.
On the pads again, Root this time works it towards mid-wicket and takes an easy single.

50 up for Rory Burns! His 6th half century in Tests! On the pads of Burns, he just nudges this one fine down the leg side and gets a single to get to the milestone. Dropped twice and he has made it count. Burns has quickly become the answer to England's opening woes. Quite consistent so far in his short Test career!
Burns goes back in his crease and blocks this one out.
Length ball on middle and off, punched the ball off the back foot.
Good length ball on the pads, worked towards the leg side.

Almost carried to the man in the deep there! Bouncer on middle and off, Burns looks to hook this one for a biggie but mistimes it. The ball falls in the empty square leg region and he takes a single. 100 up for England with this single.

Bad fielding this time! Santner is the culprit! Mitchell bowls this one full to Root, who works it towards cover. Santner there is sloppy as the ball goes off his hands towards mid off and the batters steal a run.
Root has driven this full ball superbly towards the man at mid off.
Full ball just outside off, Root opens the face of the bat and guides this one towards the man at wide first slip.
On the pads of Burns, he works this one towards mid-wicket for a single.
Good fielding! Bouncer to start of the over, Root pulls this one all along the ground towards square leg. Wagner in the deep runs to his left, dives and keeps it down to just a single.
Short delivery down the leg side, Root rocks back and pulls this one towards square leg for a single.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended out.
One of the rare occasions when Root leans forward and drives the ball with full force. However, it is hit straight to the man at cover.
Length ball just outside off, Root shoulders arms.
Again full ball on middle and off, this time Burns works it towards wide mid on and takes a single. Moves to 47 with this.
Pitched up outside off, Burns punches it towards the man at mid on.
Fullish and outside off, Root plays it with an angled bat towards the slip cordon.
Again Root prods forward and defends it out.
Root has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Bouncer just outside off, Root hops and guides this one towards the man at gully. He has to be careful while playing that shot as he was dismissed in the exact same manner in the last Test match.
Another one on middle and off, defended well.
Root prods forward to this full ball and blocks it.
On the pads of Burns,, worked towards the leg side.

Beauty by Wagner and he almost had Burns there! He bowls a full length delivery just outside off, on a driving length. Burns obliges and goes for the push but the ball grips on the surface and cuts back in. The ball sneaks through between the bat and pad of Burns and he is completely beaten. A fine diving collection by Watling there. Great cricket all around.
Full ball on middle and off, driven towards the man at mid on.
On the pads, flicked straight towards the man at mid-wicket.
Similar delivery to the previous one, pushed back towards the right of Wagner.
Fullish ball on off, Burns has defended it back towards the bowler.

FOUR! Pulled away! Back of a length ball down the leg side, Root rocks back and pulls this one through square leg for a boundary. He was in total control of that shot. These are lovely batting conditions and England are looking at ease.
Fullish this time, Root defends it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Another good length ball on middle and leg, Root pushes it back towards the bowler.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended by Root.
Fullish ball on off, Root looks to prod forward and defend but the ball goes off the inside edge onto the pads.
No ball for overstepping! On the pads, Root works this one towards the man at mid-wicket. Replays roll in and show that his foot was behind the line! Harsh one this on Daryl Mitchell.
Length ball just outside the off pole line, pushed towards the left of the bowler.
Debutant Daryl Mitchell has been given the ball now. He bowled a single over last evening and in the interview later reckoned that there is variable bounce on the pitch. Can he make use of that?

FOUR! Another half-tracker down the leg side, Burns again spots it early, gets in position and pulls it away towards the backward square leg fence. Wagner needs to mix it up here, getting too predictable at the moment.

FOUR! Hooked away! The trap is spotted by Burns and he is ready. Wagner bowls a short delivery down the leg side, Burns rocks back and uppishly plays this one towards backward square leg for a boundary.
Similar ball to the previous one, Burns again works it towards the square leg fielder. Looks like Wagner's plan is to trouble Burns with shortish balls down the leg side.
On the hips of Burns, he turns this one towards the square leg fielder.
Similar ball by Wagner, Root this time pushes this one down the ground. Williamson runs across to his right from mid off and keeps it down to a single.
Full ball on off, Root drives this one straight towards the man at cover.
Angling across the batsman, outside off, Burns allows it through.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot to the off side.
Bouncer around off, Burns leans away from the line of fire.

FOUR! Short in length and angling into the batsman, Burns gets on top of the bounce and pulls it through backward square leg for a boundary. No chance there for the fine leg fielder as it breezed away to the fence in no time.
Burns has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
